To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phosphorescence of singlet oxygen can be enhanced by localized surface plasmon resonances and that the mechanism of this enhancement appears to be the same as that which has been previously reported for the metal-enhanced fluorescence of organic molecules.
the radiative rate constant of singlet oxygen is enhanced in the presence of metal nanoparticles.

we can enhance the singlet oxygen phosphorecence by a factor of 3.5 by using a gold nanorod array and that we find that the plasmon scattering mode, rather than the plasmon absorption mode, is the key component in this process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of LSPs to enhance weak optical transitions in a molecule of choice, with an emphasis on singlet oxygen as the molecule.
the use of LSPs to enhance weak radiative transitions.
the use of metal nanoparticles and LSPs to enhance weak optical processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enhancement of phosphorescent emission from singlet oxygen is due to the coupling of the singlet oxygen emission to the LSP of a gold nanostructure.
the LSPs in the gold nanostructures are able to couple to the singlet oxygen molecule in a manner such that the rate constant for the phosphorescent decay of singlet oxygen can be increased.
LSPs from gold nanoparticles can be used to enhance the phosphorescent transition of O2(a1Δg) by up to a factor of 100.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
metal-enhanced phosphorescence can be a powerful technique for the investigation of weak optical transitions.
the use of LSPs from specially engineered gold structures provides a simple method to enhance the phosphorescence of singlet oxygen and, by implication, other phosphorescing molecules.
we have shown how metal nanoparticle-enhanced emission can be used to enhance a weak phosphorescent process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the case of singlet oxygen, LSPs can increase the radiative rate constant by a factor of ∼2.5.
metal nanoparticles can be used as an efficient means to enhance weak phosphorescent transitions, and this can be accomplished in a relatively straightforward manner.
metal nanoparticles can be used to enhance radiative transitions that are normally too weak to be observed.
